descriptors.definition: Assessees can furnish an updated return for any previous year within 24 months from the end of the relevant assessment year, regardless of whether original, belated, or revised returns were previously filed. However, updated returns are prohibited if they report a loss, decrease tax liability, result in or increase refunds, or if search, survey, or related proceedings apply.
inclusion: Returns filed within 24 months from the end of the relevant assessment year
Returns furnishing additional income
exclusion: Cases involving search, requisition, or certain surveys
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from belated returns under section 139(4) and revised returns under section 139(5) by its specific purpose of updating income with additional tax payments and strict non-applicability to loss or refund scenarios.

descriptors.definition: Before furnishing an updated return, the assessee must pay the due tax, additional income-tax, interest, and fees. Computations account for advance tax, tax deducted or collected at source, and eligible tax credits or reliefs.
inclusion: Tax payment prior to submission
Interest and fee calculations
Adjustments for TDS, TCS, and advance tax
exclusion: Returns filed without prior proof of tax and interest payment
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from regular return filing by the mandatory prepayment of an additional income-tax component alongside applicable interest and fees before submission.

descriptors.definition: The Assessing Officer may serve a notice to require a return, production of accounts and documents, or written information regarding assets and liabilities. Account production is restricted to periods not exceeding three years prior to the previous year, and asset statements require joint commissioner approval.
inclusion: Issuance of notice to furnish returns
Production of accounts and documents
Submission of written information on assets and liabilities
exclusion: Requiring accounts relating to a period more than 3 years prior to the previous year
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from summary processing under section 143(1) by involving active inquiries, document production demands, and notices issued directly by tax authorities.

descriptors.concept_name: Special Audit And Inventory Valuation Under Section 142
descriptors.definition: The Assessing Officer can direct an assessee to get accounts audited by a chartered accountant or inventory valued by a cost accountant based on account complexity, volume, doubts, or business nature. Such direction requires previous approval from specified higher income-tax authorities after providing the assessee an opportunity of being heard.
inclusion: Audit of accounts by a nominated chartered accountant
Valuation of inventory by a nominated cost accountant
exclusion: Directions issued without giving the assessee an opportunity of being heard
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from routine statutory audits by requiring specific direction from the Assessing Officer and nomination of the auditor by high-ranking tax authorities in revenue interests.

descriptors.concept_name: Power Of Assessing Officer To Make A Reference To The Valuation Officer [Section 142A]
descriptors.definition: The Assessing Officer can reference a Valuation Officer to estimate the fair market value or value of any asset, property, or investment for assessment purposes. The Valuation Officer must submit the report within six months, and the Assessing Officer utilizes it after granting the assessee a hearing opportunity.
inclusion: Reference for estimating fair market value of assets, properties, or investments
Best judgment estimation upon non-cooperation
exclusion: References made without affording an opportunity of being heard before final assessment integration
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from special audits under section 142(2A) as it focuses strictly on estimating asset, property, or investment values through a specialized Valuation Officer rather than financial account auditing.

descriptors.definition: The Central Government may notify a faceless scheme for conducting inquiries, issuing notices, ordering special audits or inventory valuations, and making valuation references. This aims to eliminate physical interfaces, optimize resource utilization through functional specialization, and introduce team-based processing with dynamic jurisdiction.
inclusion: Faceless issuance of notices
Electronic inquiries and audits
Team-based valuation references
exclusion: Physical interface processes not exempted or modified by the official notification
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from traditional physical inquiries by substituting physical interactions with an electronic, team-based framework governed by a notified Central Government scheme.

descriptors.definition: Summary assessment is a computerized preliminary processing of income returns where arithmetical errors, incorrect claims, late-filing loss set-offs, and audit report adjustments are corrected. Intimation is issued to the assessee before adjustments are finalized, allowing a response period of 30 days.
inclusion: Correction of arithmetical errors
Rectification of incorrect claims apparent from information
Disallowance of late-filed loss claims and specific deductions
exclusion: Adjustments executed without prior intimation and lapse of the 30-day response window
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from scrutiny or best judgment assessments by being an automated, preliminary computational review rather than a detailed investigative inquiry.

descriptors.concept_name: Power Of Joint Commissioner To Issue Directions In Certain Cases
descriptors.definition: A Joint Commissioner may examine pending assessment records independently, on reference, or via assessee application to issue binding guidance directions to the Assessing Officer. Prejudicial directions require prior opportunity of being heard for the assessee, excluding general investigative lines.
inclusion: Issuance of guidance directions by Joint Commissioners
Examination of pending assessment records
exclusion: Prejudicial directions issued without giving the assessee an opportunity to be heard
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from regular assessment orders by providing internal administrative guidance and binding instructions to the Assessing Officer rather than final liability determinations.

descriptors.definition: Faceless assessment conducts scrutiny, best judgment, or income escaping assessments electronically through a designated portal via automated case allocation. The National Faceless Assessment Centre coordinates responses, inquiries, and technical assistance between the assessee and specialized assessment, verification, or technical units.
inclusion: Automated allocation of cases via NFAC
Electronic responses and notices
Cross-functional coordination with verification and technical units
exclusion: Manual face-to-face assessment proceedings outside the designated electronic portal
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from traditional physical assessments by operating entirely through electronic portals with segregated functional units rather than a single local Assessing Officer.

descriptors.concept_name: Reference To Principal Commissioner Or Commissioner In Certain Cases
descriptors.definition: The Assessing Officer can refer an arrangement to the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner to declare it an impermissible avoidance arrangement. The authority issues notices, evaluates objections, and may refer the matter to an Approving Panel which issues binding directions for completion.
inclusion: References for declaring arrangements as impermissible avoidance arrangements
Approving Panel binding directions
exclusion: Arrangements finalized without giving the assessee an opportunity of being heard
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard tax evasion inquiries by targeting complex tax avoidance arrangements through a specialized multi-tier review involving the Principal Commissioner and Approving Panel.

descriptors.definition: Eligible assessees facing prejudicial variations in transfer pricing or non-resident assessments can seek alternate dispute resolution through a Dispute Resolution Panel. The panel issues binding guidance directions after reviewing draft orders and assessee objections.
inclusion: Draft assessment order forwarding for eligible assessees
Filing objections with the Dispute Resolution Panel
exclusion: Proceedings under Chapter XIV-B for search cases
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from regular assessment appeals by providing a pre-assessment fast-track collegium review mechanism specifically for eligible non-residents and transfer pricing cases.

descriptors.definition: Reassessment provisions govern the assessment of escaping income, while historical search regimes under sections 153A and 153C apply only to searches initiated on or before a specified cutoff date. Subsequent search cases are channeled into a separate block assessment framework under Chapter XIV-B.
inclusion: Reassessment of escaped income
Search assessments initiated on or before the statutory cutoff date
exclusion: Search cases initiated after the statutory cutoff date under the general reassessment sections
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard scrutiny assessments by requiring specific conditions of income escaping detection, and separated from modern search actions handled under Chapter XIV-B block assessments.
